doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Norfolk's musical families, beaches and excursions
summary: Brown describes the Cotter brothers' band and Norfolk as a musical town, with its beaches, excursion boats and Jenkins's orphanage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, that, Well, the first number I played on the trumpet when I left Hampton Institute. I knew I was getting lost in the second. I lived with the – what was those boys' names in Norfolk? Shad – there were some brothers that had a band. Shack? Not Collins. I was in California? No, no, in Norfolk, Virginia. That was Shack, that was Garfield Cotter, the Cotter boys. They were quite the good in Virginia, in Norfolk. And Garfield came from New York, you must have known Garfield, because he played with his club club. Garfield Cotter, he was the big fiddle. They were quite a musical family. They played around Norfolk.

Cotter, C-R-T-E-R, Cotter. His name was Garfield, one of the names Shack, one of the names Shag. So that's a musical family. You know, Norfolk, in the beginning, used to be quite a little town. We called it Little New York. I mean, people danced there, there was dance bands, had the old booths there, the booths there, go up to Chesapeake, I guess, on picnics. Norfolk was a Little New Orleans or a Little New York.
That's where Jenkins' home was too, wasn't it, in Norfolk?
The Arpen home that so many musicians had.
Maybe it was. I guess they were exposed to all this music. And that's how they happened to make it such an important part of the orphan training.
Maybe so. I will say that Norfolk was quite a musical town. Norfolk and Newport News. You don't hear much about those town, but they were ranked up.
They had a lot of summer excursions and such.

Oh, yes, they had plenty of it. So there was a lot of calls. And then there was Buckrow Beach and Bayshore Beach. They were kind of mostly went to Bayshore. Later on, they began to go to Buckrow Beach. It was quite a beach. Buckrow? Buckrow Beach. And you know, down in Virginia, they call it the Peninsula. There was a whole lot of water. And a whole lot of activity around there. A whole lot of activity. A whole lot. Then you get on the boat and go right up, overnight boat to Baltimore, right up to Chesapeake. And move back and forth. A lot of traffic right on the water. And then in the summertime, concerts.
